paras: Asaccus gallagheri, also known commonly as Gallagher's gecko or Gallagher's leaf-toed gecko, is a species of lizard in the family Phyllodactylidae. The species is endemic to the Arabian Peninsula and occurs in Oman and the United Arab Emirates.
The specific name, gallagheri, is in honor of zoologist Michael Desmond Gallagher (born 1921).
The preferred natural habitat of A. gallagheri is rocky areas, at altitudes from sea level to 1,700 m (5,600 ft).
A. gallagheri is oviparous. Clutch size is two eggs.
